official_sources.title: Practice guide 40 supplement 4: boundary agreements and determined boundaries

verified_facts: General boundaries are not the exact legal boundary line.
A determined boundary shows the exact line for register purposes.
Determined-boundary plans using measurements require horizontal measurements accurate to +/-10mm.
Measurements should be tied to at least two defined permanent physical features.
National Grid coordinates are an alternative requiring specialist surveying equipment.
The preferred plan scale is no smaller than 1:200.
A boundary agreement alone does not make the boundary determined.
The exact line must be established from evidence before HMLR records it as determined.
quality_effect: Prevents treating indicative HMLR polygons or title-plan edging as centimetre-accurate parcel geometry; requires determined-boundary/survey evidence for exact-line claims.
